name: TDC ADMET HIA_Hou
description: Predict whether a drug is well absorbed from the human intestine (1) or not (0) from its molecular structure, given as a SMILES string (endpoint HIA_Hou of the Therapeutics Data Commons ADMET benchmark group). The measured compounds are split by molecular scaffold into a training, a validation and a test part. The test part is fixed; the candidate is run five times (seeds 1 to 5), each time with a different division of the other compounds into training and validation. It receives the training and validation compounds with their values and the test compounds without, and returns one prediction per test compound. Each of the five runs is a separate process that receives only these arguments: it cannot read the evaluator's files, start other processes or open network connections, and it has 700 seconds. The score is the area under the ROC curve on the test compounds, averaged over the five runs; higher is better.
contract: fit_predict(train_smiles, train_y, valid_smiles, valid_y, test_smiles, info) -> sequence of finite numbers, one per test molecule in the given order: a score that is larger for class 1 (for example its probability). train_smiles, valid_smiles and test_smiles are lists of SMILES strings, train_y and valid_y lists of numbers; info has name, metric, kind ('regression' or 'binary') and seed. Score: mean over the seeds 1 to 5 of the area under the ROC curve on the test part, maximized.
notes: Downloaded by PyTDC at first use into data/admet
Predicts the binary human-intestinal-absorption class (1 = absorbed) of 578 drugs from their SMILES strings, scored by AUROC.
Leaders are large tuned ensembles or foundation-model fine-tunes.
Needs PyTDC and rdkit: not in .venv-tasks, so the evaluator restarts itself under tools/venv-admet (created by the README's setup steps).

Every scoring call of the candidate runs in the main suite's sandbox (a child process with an audit hook, 700 s and 6 GB for one call): it keeps a search from coming across the test labels and is not a security boundary against a candidate written to attack the evaluator.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Classify drug molecules as well or poorly absorbed from the human gut (human intestinal absorption) from their structure.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: A drug given by mouth must be absorbed through the intestine to act, so predicting absorption early removes poorly absorbed candidates from development.
